issues.problem: The whole test class looks like decompiler output, not source code. It uses 3-space indentation and K&R braces where the rest of the project uses 4-space Allman style. It has synthetic labels and flags (`label211`, `label203`, `var10001`), redundant casts like `(Block)ModBlocks.HEMP_CROP.get()`, `(BlockState)((BlockState)...setValue(...))`, `(Integer)`, `(Boolean)`, `(ResourceKey)` and `(Named)`, and fully qualified `net.minecraft.world.level.block.Blocks` names because of an import clash with `TFCTags.Blocks`.
issues.reason: The code style asks for small, direct and readable code. The synthetic control flow and redundant casts hide what each assertion checks and do not match the project's formatting.
issues.fix: Rewrite the class in the project style: 4-space Allman formatting and no redundant casts. Replace the labelled blocks with direct `instanceof` pattern checks inside `helper.assertTrue`. Import `TFCTags` and refer to `TFCTags.Blocks.CAN_BE_SNOW_PILED` so that `net.minecraft.world.level.block.Blocks` can be imported normally.

issues.problem: Every pool gets the same explicit name `loot_pool`, so `crop/hemp` and `wild_crop/hemp` each contain two pools with the same name (see the generated `loot_table/blocks/crop/hemp.json`).
issues.reason: NeoForge identifies pools by name (`LootTable.getPool` / `removePool` in `LootTableLoadEvent`), so duplicate names within one table make pool lookups ambiguous for other mods and data packs. The explicit name is also unnecessary, because NeoForge gives unnamed pools unique default names.
issues.fix: Remove `.name("loot_pool")` from the `pool` helper and regenerate the loot tables with runData.

history.note: fixed: Removed the explicit loot_pool name and regenerated all hemp loot tables with unique default pool names.

issues.problem: The configured features, placed features and the `#tfc:feature/crops` tag are built as hand-assembled Gson objects in a custom `DataProvider`. Nothing passes through the vanilla codecs, which is why the `would_survive` predicate type is written without a namespace.
issues.reason: The code style says to use vanilla and NeoForge mechanisms before custom code. NeoForge's `DatapackBuiltinEntriesProvider` (with a `RegistrySetBuilder` for `CONFIGURED_FEATURE`/`PLACED_FEATURE`) and a `TagsProvider<PlacedFeature>` produce these files from typed objects and validate them through the registry codecs.
issues.fix: Replace `HempWorldgenProvider` with a `DatapackBuiltinEntriesProvider`. It should register `tfie:plant/wild_crop/hemp` (TFC tall_wild_crop with `BlockConfig` of the wild block) and `tfie:plant/wild_crop/hemp_patch` (`RandomPatchConfiguration(6, 5, 1, ...)`), plus the placed features with `HeightmapPlacement`/`BlockPredicateFilter` (TFC replaceable, `BlockPredicate.wouldSurvive`), `RarityFilter.onAverageOnceEvery(90)`, `InSquarePlacement` and TFC's climate placement. Add the patch to `tfc:feature/crops` with a `TagsProvider` for `Registries.PLACED_FEATURE`, then regenerate.

history.note: fixed: Replaced hand-built Gson worldgen with DatapackBuiltinEntriesProvider, typed configured/placed features, codec-backed predicates and climate placement, plus a TagsProvider for #tfc:feature/crops.

issues.problem: The screenshot shows none of the cultivated Hemp stages (age 0–4) or the dead and wild plants sitting on soil. Every soil spot is an empty one-block hole in the quartz platform. Dropped seed items float next to most holes, so the planted bottoms broke. The only plants visible are a few separate green and yellow tops floating above the back row with no lower half under them. You can't check the per-age models, the missing top at age 0–3, or how the mature top and bottom line up.
issues.reason: tests/e2e/hemp-rendering.mjs:17 and :30 use `tfc:farmland/entisol` and `tfc:dirt/entisol`. TFC 4.2.16 has no `entisol` soil type (its soils are loam, silt, sandy_loam and silty_loam). Both setblock commands fail and leave air under the crops, and the crop bottoms drop as items when their neighbours update. The setup never builds the scene the Expected Result needs. The floating tops without bottoms are also a side effect of this broken setup, not a valid mature two-block plant.
issues.fix: Use real TFC soil blocks, for example `tfc:farmland/loam` for the cultivated row and `tfc:dirt/loam` (or `tfc:grass/loam`) for the dead and wild row. Place the soil before each bottom and its top, and check that every setblock succeeds (for example with `execute if block`) before taking the screenshot. Then the screenshot can show age 0–4, immature and mature dead plants, and immature and mature wild plants on their soil.

history.note: fixed: Replaced nonexistent entisol blocks with tfc:farmland/loam and tfc:dirt/loam, placed support before every crop half, removed stale dropped items, and added MC Pilot read-back checks for every fixture block before screenshots.

No mature plant is complete, so you can't judge whether the halves line up, whether faces overlap, or whether the transparent parts of the leaves render correctly.
issues.reason: This screenshot comes from the same setup, which uses soil IDs that don't exist (`tfc:farmland/entisol` and `tfc:dirt/entisol`), so every bottom half lost its support and dropped. Frame the cultivated age-4 plant (z=1) and the mature wild and dead plants (z=5) so both halves and the leaf cutouts fill a large part of the frame.
